# KKT — Kitty Kat Technologies

> Senior PMO and AI delivery for mid-sized retailers ($50M–$500M) and fuel networks. Based in Tallinn, Estonia (EU). We build and ship operating systems, not decks. Marquee deployment: Optimus, live at Alfa Oil — 600+ stations, $500M annual revenue, Kyrgyzstan.

Kitty Kat Technologies OÜ (public brand: KKT) is an AI delivery and programme-management firm registered in Tallinn, Estonia. The firm works with mid-sized retailers and fuel networks across Central Europe, the EU, and Central Asia. Every engagement starts with a two-week diagnostic. Delivery follows a three-stage model: strengthen the core, optimize and grow, expand and monetize. The exit criterion — the system runs without KKT — is written into the engagement from week one.

The flagship product is Optimus, an operating-intelligence system for fuel-distribution networks. Each morning Optimus pulls live ERP data, forecasts when each station and fuel-type position will hit critical level, detects inbound delivery conflicts, and produces concrete procurement recommendations: which supplier, how many tons, by what date, at what price. It is live at two deployments — Alfa Oil (600+ stations, $500M revenue, Kyrgyzstan) and a second Central Asian network (10 stations, 11 fuel types, 3 regions).

KKT avoids vendor-hype language. Outcomes are stated in measurable terms — margin, cash, availability, customer value, productivity — or not stated at all. The firm is candid about poor fit: it turns down work below ~$50M revenue, pure strategy without delivery, engagements with no senior internal owner, regulated banking/public-sector/defence work, and full outsourcing.

- [Alfa Oil case study](https://kittykat.tech/case-studies/alfa-oil/): Fuel retail, Kyrgyzstan. 600+ stations, $500M annual revenue, 11 fuel types. Optimus live in production.
- [Click & Grow case study](https://kittykat.tech/case-studies/click-and-grow/): B2C smart indoor gardens. Customer analytics and ML segmentation for Eastern Europe / CIS growth.
- [GTE case study](https://kittykat.tech/case-studies/gte/): Industrial compressor manufacturer. Finance/manufacturing reporting plus ML for anomaly detection and energy-consumption optimisation.
- [Kricon case study](https://kittykat.tech/case-studies/kricon/): International logistics. Operational visibility — reporting infrastructure, anomaly detection, and clustering models.
- [CSC Telecom case study](https://kittykat.tech/case-studies/csc-telecom/): Mid-sized telecom provider. Customer and product analytics; several insights adopted and shipped.
- [Cost of Doing Nothing — methodology](https://kittykat.tech/methods/cost-of-doing-nothing/): A public, dated methodology (v0.1, 2026-05-07) for a fuel-retail P&L gap calculator. Seven principles; five benchmark source tiers including public annual reports (MOL, OMV, Couche-Tard, EG Group, Shell, BP, ENI) and KKT internal aggregated benchmarks (2022–2026, minimum n=5).
